title: Activate ollama-route-pretooluse auto-mode + unify telemetry so file-read offloads are measurable
brief: Targets a DIFFERENT pathway than OLLAMA-EXPAND-MS0/the existing offload dashboard. The dashboard's 6.9% lifetime / 5.9% last-48h-adjusted figures come from `ollama-task-offloader` (UserPromptSubmit hook) — and 49 of the last-48h keeps are correctly-kept Claude orchestration prompts (/checkin, /loop, /goal, operator directives, deep_reasoning). Those keeps SHOULD stay on Claude — Ollama can't generate Claude's response. The 32 'unknown' keeps in the same window are nearly all the same conversational prompt repeated across sessions, also correctly kept. So the prompt-router rate is healthier than the headline suggests, and U1 will NOT move that number much. THIS milestone targets a separate leakage path: every time Claude reads a >24KB data-state JSON / log / report file, the existing PreToolUse:Read hook `ollama-route-pretooluse.mjs` fires an advisory but Claude (me + every other slot) ignores it and loads the raw bytes anyway. The hook supports an auto-substitute mode (env `PRISM_OLLAMA_ROUTE_AUTO=1`) that would deny the raw Read and inject an Ollama summary — but that mode is OFF by default and nothing in the repo flips it on. AND, critically, the file-read offloads have their OWN telemetry sink (`.claude/cache/hook-telemetry.jsonl`) that the dashboard does NOT read — so even if we flip the switch today we can't tell whether it worked. U1 ships activation + telemetry unification together (they're useless apart); U2 perf-tunes Ollama; U3/U4 are conditional follow-ups gated on real measurements.

revision_history.note: Initial envelope. FAILED per-file scrutiny: P0 — 32-unknown-keeps claim conflated prompt-router leakage with file-read leakage; P0 — U1's success was unmeasurable without U5 telemetry unification first.

Brief rewritten to separate the two pathways. U1+U5 merged into single P0 (activation+measurement ship together). R2 mitigation tightened to require post-parse range checks (minKb >= 8, mode enum, model allowlist). R12 fail-loud strengthened: substitute banner now requires explicit [OLLAMA-SUBSTITUTE sha256:... bytes=N model=...] header, not a passive emoji. U2 rollback added. ROI math added in U1 description.

U2 SHIPPED (iter 5). Added 4 Ollama perf env vars to docker-compose.yml ollama service (KEEP_ALIVE=-1 / FLASH_ATTENTION=1 / KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 / NUM_PARALLEL=4). Recreated container via `docker compose up -d ollama` — R12 fail-loud: `docker compose restart` was tried first and DID NOT pick up the new env (env block is baked at container creation, not at start). Verified via `docker inspect prism-ollama | grep OLLAMA_` — all 4 vars applied + container Up 2 minutes (healthy) + /api/tags returns qwen2.5-coder:7b model loaded. Also flipped ollama-route-config.json mode 'suggest'->'auto' — telemetry pre-check confirmed `byHook.ollama-route-pretooluse.fired=177` row populated in ollama-offload-stats.json, satisfying U1 Reviewer B P0 safe-rollout gate. completed_units 1->2; status remains in_progress (U3/U4 are conditional/deferred).

created_by_notes: Created in /loop iter 1 after a fresh post-compact GPU/Docker/Ollama probe. The prior summary said GPU was VRAM-bound (73% used) — the LIVE probe at envelope-write time shows 27% VRAM / 48% compute (12GB headroom). VRAM is NOT the constraint right now; routing visibility + activation is. duplicationGuardEngine: checked INTEL-OLLAMA-OBSIDIAN-MS0/MS1 + OLLAMA-EXPAND-MS0 — none of them touch the PreToolUse:Read auto-mode env var (PRISM_OLLAMA_ROUTE_AUTO) and none unify the file-read telemetry into the offload dashboard. Hidden-coupling check: `grep -rln PRISM_OLLAMA_ROUTE_AUTO H:/prism/.claude/ H:/prism/scripts/ H:/prism/mcp-server/src/` returns only the hook itself + its test file — no split-brain risk from the env-vs-config fallback (R2 mitigation holds).

real_state_snapshot_at_creation.regression_clarification: OLLAMA-EXPAND-MS0/U-OE-DASH-KEEP-BREAKDOWN recorded 'raw 10.9% lifetime -> 42.1% last-24h adjusted' at its 2026-05-18 ship — those are prompt-router (`ollama-task-offloader`) figures. Today's prompt-router figures are 6.9% raw lifetime / 5.9% adjusted 48h. Apples-to-apples comparison: adjusted rate did regress (42.1% adj -> 5.9% adj) — but the adjusted-rate denominator depends on what's classified as `correctly-kept` vs `unknown`, and the recent fleet activity is dominated by orchestration directives (/checkin-X, /loop, /goal across 26 slots), which inflates the correctly-kept share and shrinks the headroom available for genuine offload. THIS MILESTONE does not target prompt-router; it targets the orthogonal file-read pathway whose telemetry is invisible to the dashboard today.
real_state_snapshot_at_creation.file_read_offload_telemetry_today: ollama-route-pretooluse hook writes to `.claude/cache/hook-telemetry.jsonl` (separate from `ollama-offload-stats.json`). Without reading both files manually we cannot tell whether file-read advisories are firing OR whether anyone is acting on them. U1 unifies.

units.title: Activate ollama-route-pretooluse auto-mode + unify its telemetry into ollama-offload-stats.json
deliverables: Modify `.claude/hooks/ollama-route-pretooluse.mjs` to add a repo-scoped config-file fallback: read `mcp-server/data/state/ollama-route-config.json` (schema: `{mode:'auto'|'suggest', minKb:number, model:string}`) when the corresponding env vars are unset. Env STILL wins (precedence preserved for callers that already set env). Export a pure `loadRouteConfig({configPath})` so it's unit-testable.

POST-PARSE schema validation in `loadRouteConfig`: (a) `mode` must be exactly 'auto' OR 'suggest' (enum) — anything else falls back to 'suggest'; (b) `minKb` must be an integer >= 8 (a malicious 0 or 1 would route EVERY read, denial-of-Claude-context attack — see R2); (c) `model` must match `/^[\w./:-]{1,64}$/` AND match a name returned by `GET /api/tags` (verified once per hook process, cached for process-lifetime — acceptable because hook processes are short-lived). Invalid mode/minKb values silently fall back to safe defaults with a single warning line to the telemetry log (R12). CASCADE-FAILURE CLARIFICATION (added per scrutiny v1.0.1): if `GET /api/tags` ITSELF fails (Ollama down, timeout, network error) so the allowlist check cannot complete, the hook MUST short-circuit to raw-Read pass-through — NOT to 'substitute with the default model' (which would itself fail the same check and silently degrade) and NOT to suggest-mode (which would still write an advisory the caller might ignore). Raw Read is the only correct fail-open path when allowlist verification itself is broken. Emit one telemetry warning per process documenting the cascade.

Modify the auto-mode substitute message (`runRoute` lines ~198-200) to lead with a FAIL-LOUD banner: `[OLLAMA-SUBSTITUTE model=<model> sha256=<sha256-of-source-file-first-48KB> bytes=<actual-file-bytes> route=auto]\n\n<summary>`. Replace the passive `📄` emoji header. Operator/Claude must be able to detect (via grep) that an offload happened and audit which file was substituted.
Ship `mcp-server/data/state/ollama-route-config.json` with `{"mode":"auto","minKb":24,"model":"qwen2.5-coder:7b"}` — flips repo-wide on the next hook fire in a new shell.

TELEMETRY UNIFICATION (this was previously a separate U5): extend `ollama-route-pretooluse.mjs` to ALSO append to `mcp-server/data/state/ollama-offload-stats.json` (atomic RMW per existing pattern in `ollama-task-offloader.mjs`) on every fire — `byHook.ollama-route-pretooluse = {fired, offloaded, kept, suggested, tokensSaved}`. Without this, the dashboard cannot see file-read offloads and U1's success cannot be measured. Existing `.claude/cache/hook-telemetry.jsonl` log retained as a per-event audit trail.

Add 9 new test cases in `.claude/hooks/ollama-route-pretooluse.test.mjs`: (1) config absent → defaults preserved, (2) config present + env unset → config wins, (3) config present + env set → env wins (precedence), (4) corrupt config JSON → fail-open to suggest mode + warning logged, (5) config with `minKb:0` → schema rejects, falls back to default 24, (6) config with `mode:'whatever'` → schema rejects, falls back to suggest, (7) auto mode + Ollama timeout → fail-open to raw Read (preserves existing fail-open invariant), (8) source-file Read still passes through (SRC_EXT exemption intact), (9) substitute banner contains `[OLLAMA-SUBSTITUTE` + `sha256=` + `bytes=` markers.
acceptance: On a fresh PowerShell, reading a >24KB file under `mcp-server/data/state/` results in `permissionDecision: deny` + a substitute message starting with `[OLLAMA-SUBSTITUTE model=qwen2.5-coder:7b sha256=... bytes=...]` — NOT raw bytes loaded into Claude context.
On a source-file Read (.ts/.mjs/.py/etc) at any size: hook passes through (no offload).
`grep '"hook":"ollama-route-pretooluse"' H:/prism/mcp-server/data/state/ollama-offload-stats.json` returns at least one event within 24h of activation.
Dashboard (`node scripts/ollama-offload-dashboard.mjs --window=48h`) shows a NEW row `ollama-route-pretooluse` in the `Per-hook fire counts` section with `offload > 0`.
Fail-open invariants intact: Ollama down → Read proceeds (no test failures); config corrupt → suggest mode (verified by integration test).

Schema-validation invariants: a malicious `{"mode":"auto","minKb":0}` in the config file does NOT cause the hook to route 0-byte reads (verified by integration test that writes that config, fires the hook, asserts pass-through).
units.roi_math: Back-of-envelope: across 26 fleet slots, a conservative 5 large-bulk-data reads/day/slot × 24KB-avg × ~6k tokens/read = ~130k tokens/day saved (~3.9M tokens/month) IF activation propagates. Build cost (this unit + scrutiny): ~50-100k tokens one-time. Break-even in <24h fleet activity. Smaller if my read-rate estimate is high — U1's telemetry unification is exactly the measurement that proves or disproves this.
units.scrutiny_required: per-file (2 reviewers per file × 4 files: hook patch + config file + test patch + this envelope revision); 3-of-3 Stop gate.
units.rollback: Set `{"mode":"suggest"}` in `mcp-server/data/state/ollama-route-config.json` OR delete the file. Reversible in seconds. No system/shell state to clean up. To roll back the telemetry-unification: comment out the new `byHook.ollama-route-pretooluse` append in the hook (dashboard will keep showing the hook row but with stale counts until reset).

acceptance: U1 shipped (lever + measurement together); within 48h of U1 ship the dashboard shows a non-zero `byHook.ollama-route-pretooluse.offloaded` count AND a substitute message containing `[OLLAMA-SUBSTITUTE` is observable in at least one chat session; within 7d the file-read offload column shows steady-state >5 offloads/day across the fleet. U2 shipped if it measurably reduces cold-call latency. U3/U4 closed as `shipped` or `not-needed` with the measurement that proves the decision.

risks.description: Auto-substitute hides bytes Claude actually needed — summary loses a key fact and Claude makes wrong decision downstream.
risks.mitigation: U1 deliverable: substitute message banner `[OLLAMA-SUBSTITUTE model=... sha256=... bytes=N route=auto]` is grep-able + tells Claude how to retry via offset/limit. Source-file Reads bypassed by SRC_EXT exemption. Only triggers on bulk-data paths (state/data/state/logs/etc). Telemetry unification (U1) lets us spot quality issues by spot-checking substituted-vs-kept ratio on the same file path; if a path is substituted then Claude retries it raw, that's a quality-failure signal.

risks.description: Config-file write surface — `mcp-server/data/state/` is written by 20+ slot/hook processes. Any of them could write a malicious `ollama-route-config.json` to DENY all reads of state files via `{mode:auto, minKb:0}` — a DoS-by-route attack that's VALID-shape (passes naïve schema check) but pathological.
risks.mitigation: U1 deliverable explicitly requires post-parse RANGE validation: `minKb >= 8` (integer), `mode` matches enum `auto|suggest`, `model` matches `/^[\w./:-]{1,64}$/` AND is present in `GET /api/tags`. Out-of-range values silently fall back to safe defaults with a warning to the telemetry log (R12: surface the silent-fallback). Hook ALSO fail-OPENs on corrupt JSON / missing file — both safer than denying reads.

risks.description: Cold-start lag — first Ollama call after warm-loss adds 5-9s. 26+ slots reading simultaneously could queue and time out.
risks.mitigation: Hook timeout is 9s and fails-OPEN to raw Read. U2 sets KEEP_ALIVE=-1 (model stays resident). U2 also sets NUM_PARALLEL to handle concurrent slots. Worst case: a few reads slip through to Claude during cold-start — same as today.

risks.description: ROI estimate uncertainty — the 130k tokens/day saved figure assumes ~5 bulk-data reads/day/slot. If the actual rate is much lower (e.g., the fleet mostly reads source files which are exempt), the milestone may be net-neutral on token economy.
risks.mitigation: U1's telemetry unification IS the measurement. Within 7d we'll know the actual rate. If <50 offloads/day fleet-wide, deprioritize U2/U3/U4 and close the milestone with the empirical finding (still valuable: it proves where the offload opportunity is NOT).
